chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Ma'ruf ibn Kharbuz, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: There is no believer who is afflicted with a calamity in the world and then utters the phrase of return (Istirja') at the time of his calamity until the calamity strikes him, except that Allah will forgive him all of his sins that have passed, except the greater sins for which Allah has made Hell obligatory. He said: And whenever he remembers a future calamity in his lifespan and utters the phrase of return at it and praises Allah, Allah will forgive him every sin he acquired between the first utterance of Istirja' and the second, except the greater sins among the sins.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for a believer who utters Istirja' during calamities according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) elucidates that uttering the Istirja' upon a calamity expiates minor sins, while consistent remembrance and gratitude for future trials serve as a continuous mechanism for forgiveness between events. This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, highlights the spiritual efficacy of patience (sabr) and active remembrance (dhikr) in maintaining a state of divine grace, distinguishing between general forgiveness and the specific exclusion of major sins (al-Kaba'ir) that require distinct repentance. It underscores the Shia emphasis on the transformative power of conscious response to adversity as a means of spiritual purification.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) said, “If a believer faces a calamity in this world and utters Laa ilaaha illallaah, Allah will forgive all of his sins except the greater sins for which the  punishment  of  Hell  is  obligatory.

Utter  Laa  ilaaha illallaah  and glorify Allah whenever you are faced with a calamity in future. In this case Allah will forgive all the sins committed  between  two  utterances  (of  the  above  phrase) except greater sins.”
